title: Is There a Causal Relation between Maternal Acetaminophen Administration and ADHD?
ehr_evidence: The study used a murine model; 'Pregnant CD1 mice (N = 8/group) were allocated to receive by gavage either APAP (150 mg/kg/day...) or 0.5% carboxymethylcellulose (control group),' with outcomes assessed via ELISA, MRI, and histology rather than electronic health records.
summary: In a controlled murine model, prenatal acetaminophen administration at the FDA-approved maximum human dose did not cause hyperkinetic dysfunction or ADHD-like behavioral, anatomical, or histological abnormalities in mouse offspring.
key_findings: No significant differences in any locomotor activity parameter (total locomotor activity, rearing, central vs peripheral time, fine repetitive movements, total ambulation) between groups at the P<0.008 threshold.
No significant differences in volumes of 29 brain areas of interest on 11.7 Tesla MRI between the APAP and control groups.
No significant difference in cortical neuron density of Nissl-stained frontal cortex between groups (p<0.05; unpaired Student's t-test; n=5 control, n=3 treated).
No difference in maternal serum ALT concentrations between groups (ED7: 11.2 vs 11.7, P=0.3; ED18: 11.7 vs 12.7, P=0.5), indicating no hepatotoxicity.
Maternal serum APAP concentration peaked at 30 minutes after gavage, reaching a mean of 117 μg/ml.
Findings do not support a causal relationship between prenatal APAP exposure and hyperkinetic dysfunction/ADHD.
captured_features: Time spent in central vs peripheral enclosure areas
Volumes of 29 brain areas on MRI
population: Pregnant CD1 (Swiss) mice and their offspring (murine model)
limitations: No established animal model for ADHD, so no positive control was available for comparison.
Oral gavage itself may act as a stressor that could mask differences between groups.
No 24-hour home cage activity monitoring, which may better fit ADHD diagnostic criteria.
Narrow focus on hyperkinetic behavior only, without investigating inattention, impulsivity, or emotional dysregulation.
Results should be interpreted with caution when compared to clinical human data due to lack of accurate ADHD assessment in murine models.
data_availability_statement: All relevant data are within the paper and its Supporting Information files.
